newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 7.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - July 7.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:
NEW DELHI - Ogilvy & Mather Worldwide, part of London-based WPP Group, reaches agreement to buy Speer Advertising in India.

PARIS - French media and communications group Havas signs deal with Publicis, the advertising, direct marketing and PR firm, under which Havas will sell its 50-percent stake in Metrobus and 33.3-percent in Mediavision. Metrobus manages the advertising on the Paris metro system and Mediavision is France's leading broker of advertising space in cinemas.

SYDNEY - Coca-Cola South Pacific has shifted its Australian soft drink Lift account from The Campaign Palace, part of the Bates group, to Mojo Partners Sydney, which already handles Powerade, Sprite, Diet Sprite and Coke sports sponsorship as well as media planning on non-Coke brands.

LONDON - Mirror Group Plc, the British newspaper publisher, says its advertising revenues are comfortably ahead of the first half of last year. Mirror, which has agreed to acquire Midland Independent Newspapers for 297 million pounds ($502.2 million), also says its LIVE TV cable television channels has recorded "impressive viewing and market share figures".
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt calls for the removal of restrictions on encryption technology, kicking off a two-day conference on Internet commerce attended by 40 government ministers from the European Union, the United States, Russia, Japan and Canada.
PARIS - French private television station M6-Metropole Television is rated as the most popular general channel, overtaking its bigger and older rivals, according to Strategies magazine.

LONDON - The price of shares in British Sky Broadcasting Plc fell on the London Stock Exchange after a weekend report said Rupert Murdoch, chairman of News Corp -- which owns 40 percent of Sky shares -- described the stock as overpriced.

KUALA LUMPUR - From Web pages on the Internet to electronic shopping malls featuring local goods, corporations are nudging into Asia with business products and solutions tailored for the region, say industry experts.

BONN - Bertelsmann AG, Europe's biggest media conglomerate, says Thomas Middelhoff, the man who's driven the company's move into multimedia and Internet-related services, will become chairman next year.
JAKARTA - Indonesia's parliament plans to re-examine a broadcasting bill that was passed by the house last year, according to local reports.

BERLIN - German regional television station Puls-TV, in the midst of bankruptcy proceedings, says it is laying off 64 employees and will let the last 60 go at the end of August. Attorney Wolfgang Schroeder, who is overseeing the proceedings, says the channel will continue to be backed until the end of August by newly founded station TV Berlin, owned by Thomas Kirch, son of media mogul Leo Kirch.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
SHANGHAI - MasterCard International officially opens a representative office in Shanghai to help gain a share of China's growing market for payment cards.

LONDON - Vodafone Group Plc, Britain's biggest mobile telephone company, plans to unveil a new corporate identity which will include getting rid of most of its 12 separate brands and introducing a unified billing system.
NEW DELHI - The Indian government has approved an investment by U.S. soft drink maker Coca-Cola Company to set up bottling plants under an overall $700 million investment plan, industry sources say.

TOKYO - Sony Corp and Nintendo Co Ltd are becoming the two dominant giants in the game machine market with Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd seen pulling out of the development of a next-generation 64-bit game console, analysts say.

SYDNEY - Australian new motor vehicle sales rose 18.8 percent in June, and sales in the first six months of 1997 are 6.2 percent above sales for the same period for 1996, the Federal Chamber of Automotive Industries says.
HONG KONG - Hong Kong says it expects over 12 million tourists this year, spending $US12.27 billion, retaining its place as East Asia's top tourist destination.
CONSUMER TRENDS:
BEIJING - Most urban Chinese residents plan to buy their own homes instead of waiting for their work units to allocate houses to them, the Overseas Edition of the People's Daily says.

PARIS - The latest fashion from Paris is clothing containing human body parts according to a report in the Sunday Times. Alexander McQueen, who designs for Givenchy, has been accused by competitors of trying to recycle bits of human bone and blood in his new collection.

BONN - The consumption of beef in Germany declined by nearly 10 percent in 1996 as Germans opted for fowl, according to German agriculture ministry. The per-capita beef consumption in Germany declined by nearly one kg to 10.5 kg, while fowl was up 400 grams to 8.4 kg per capita.
BEIJING - Demand for organic food in China is outstripping supply, despite a 71.4 percent rise in production last year the China Business Daily says.

ROME - Italy is a land of chronic liars according to a survey published by Riza Psicosomatica, a monthly psychology review. It said 70 percent of Italian men and women interviewed confessed to telling between five and 10 lies every day. "Don't worry about it. It's all been taken care of," is the most common lie told, the publication says.
